info.title: The newitem modal — the contract between a GroupObject type and its `+`
info.summary: What a kind asks for when you create one, written from the surface that asks it.
description: ONE component serves every mint (app/ui/App/Design/New.swift). It contains no `switch kind`:
the TYPE declares its initialisation fields (pacific-core/src/mint.rs) and the surface renders
them. This document is the contract between those two halves — what a declaration may say, and
what the surface guarantees in return.
It exists because the two used to be independent statements of one fact and had drifted in four
places at once, each of them a field you could type into and have silently dropped.

surface.summary: What the modal is, independent of kind.

faces.fields: The declared fields, in declaration order.
faces.visibility: The audience dial, reached from GOLD. Common to every kind including the note; the gold glow swaps to cyan. The card TURNS rather than being covered.

buttons.summary: The modal carries NO buttons of its own. Its three actions are the shell's own RED/GOLD/BLUE circles, which slide out of their neutral arrangement and become them. This is why a newitem modal is a shell overlay and never a sheet: a sheet sits above the shell and cannot borrow those circles.
buttons.red: Cancel. Always live. Warns first when there is anything to lose.
buttons.gold: Visibility. Always live — the audience is answerable before the object has a name.
buttons.blue: Commit. Live exactly when every REQUIRED field is answered and no commit is in flight.

surface.dismissal: Tapping off the canvas is the same action as RED: an empty surface goes, one with content asks first.
surface.focus: Nothing is selected on open, so the keyboard stays down until a field is chosen. The note is the exception — it is a single box to type in.

inputs.summary: Each input names a CONTROL, not a kind. This is what makes the renderer total: the surface never asks which kind it is drawing.

line.chrome: the DM composer's own slot — disc-radius corner, surface2, hairline
line.label: CENTRED INSIDE the box, clearing on focus and returning when emptied

place.label: inline, TRAILING — WHERE reads from the right of its selector

fix.control: READOUT of the device's live coordinate, never a picker
fix.label: above

icon.control: circular media slot, tap to open the camera
icon.label: none

banner.control: wide media slot, tap to open the camera
banner.label: none

rows.summary: Declaration order is row order, with exactly one grouping rule.
rows.media: An `icon` immediately followed by a `banner` becomes ONE media row with no caption — two slots and a camera say what they are. An unpaired icon still gets its own row; it is never dropped for want of a partner.
rows.ceiling: A mint is the START of an object, not a form to complete. The ceiling lives in the declaration, where the judgement belongs.
rows.order: NAME first, then MEDIA, then DESCRIBE, then the kind's own switches, then WHERE. Confirmed against the declaration, which is what the surface renders — this is the shape, not a coincidence of listing.

vocabulary.summary: A `choice` field carries the REDUCER'S OWN wire values, so a picker can never mint a value the fold will reject.
vocabulary.narrowing: The surface MAY offer a SUBSET of the declared values, and MAY show a different word for one. Offering fewer of the reducer's own values is always safe; the wire word is not always the word to show.
vocabulary.forbidden: The surface may NOT offer a value the declaration does not carry, and may not send a word in place of a value.

examples.thing.category: declared artifact|skill|job; offered artifact|skill, with `artifact` shown as “Thing”
examples.thing.stance: offered offers|wants for a thing, has|wants for a skill; `wants` reads WANT of a thing and NEED of a skill

carriage.summary: Every declared field states how it reaches the object. This is the promise the contract exists to keep.
carriage.op0: Lands in the kind's op-0 profile delta. `fields_carry_to_the_wire` proves each one arrives.
carriage.separate: Rides its own delta after the mint — the media ops, a Place's fix, an Event's venue. Named in `every_separate_field_is_actually_delivered`, so the flag cannot become a way to silence the first test.
carriage.deferred: SHOWN AND NOT YET SAVED. A stated fact, never a silent drop; enumerated in `deferred_fields_are_the_known_placeholders`. A required field may never be deferred — that would gate the commit on something that cannot be kept.
carriage.dependent: A field whose delivery depends on ANOTHER field's value is only honest while the surface can actually produce that value. `thing.price` is refused by `thing.setPosture` unless the stance is ACTIVE (buying|selling), and the offered stance vocabulary is deliberately offers|wants|has — so no choice a person can make would let a price be kept. It is therefore declared `deferred`, not `separate`: the row is the design, the claim that it saves would be false. When an active stance becomes offerable it becomes `separate` and nothing else changes.

commit.rule: Every field the type declares `required` is answered, and no commit is in flight. Nothing else gates it.
commit.answered: Text is trimmed, so whitespace is not an answer. A date is answered by any NON-ZERO instant — 0 is the sentinel that minted events in 1970. A fix is answered by having one.
commit.failure: A commit that returns no outcome leaves the surface up with its content intact. A mint that did not happen must never look like one that did.

notMinted.summary: Kinds with no `+`, and why — so an absence is a decision rather than an oversight.
notMinted.contact: formed by PAIRING, a double opt-in; one side cannot mint it
notMinted.conversation: formed by consuming a Contact's prekeys
notMinted.system: has a reducer but no ICD channel and no product surface
notMinted.field: declared in ObjectKind with no ObjectType impl
notMinted.topic: declared in ObjectKind with no ObjectType impl
notMinted.transaction: opened by the settler, who adds the buyer and the seller and fixes their roles; a party asks for one, and never mints it
